Derived from the saved aircraft geometry. Both spars stay attached at BL 1280. The straight lines extend the first outboard spar segment inboard. C is the closest studied interpretation of George's sketch.
Calculated study mass ledger. The frame proxies pass the selected local buckling screen but fail the stress screen. These are not equal-strength released part weights.
Calculated cover, spar-web, and cap gauges. Every step occurs at a modeled rib. Runouts, gauge transitions, local joints, fatigue, and manufacturing details require a later design pass.
Calculated in-plane stress on 8 mm target meshes. Circles locate maximum element stresses. The common color scale extends to 550 MPa. The 250 MPa study ceiling is exceeded in both forward frames.

Calculated station sweep. The aft primary stays at FS 5400 for this curve. Blue includes the least-mass bracing allowance. Gray omits that additional bracing. Every forward-frame stress result exceeds the study ceiling.

The wing is re-sized for each load, cover-pitch, or load-line case. Baseline frame gauges remain fixed in these sensitivity totals; their stresses scale with the applied load. The plot is not a set of fully re-sized aircraft weights.

Calculated pad-to-inner-flange rib layout at the current primary stations. Orange lines identify the eight paths per primary. The exterior, main opening, and all passage envelopes stay fixed in this candidate.
Revision F native nTop view of the updated primaries and hat longerons. All eight pads per primary connect to the inner flange. Primary stations and the central opening remain fixed.
Measured plan-view comparison of existing cranked spar routes and straight inboard extensions
Calculated stress from the two-dimensional model. The displayed factored stresses are linear extrapolations. Values above the assumed ceiling do not represent a valid elastic material response.

Pocket-floor screening factors at the factored load, after the assumed 0.65 reduction. The required factor is 1.15. Green regions are candidates for closer local study, not approval to remove material.
Uniform rib and web trials. Labels give rib width r and residual web thickness w in millimetres. Mass is a projected membrane proxy that omits the three-dimensional blend volume.
Measured baseline dimensions and proposed section dimensions at the same scale. These are straight-section shapes, not complete curved ribs.

Discrete section search using the recovered baseline force envelopes. A ratio above one means more material per unit length. No passing option means the search cannot support a thickness recommendation.
Native nTop section coupons. Blue shows the flat rib references; orange shows the thin flanged candidates. Gold shows the hat concept and gray shows the solid round reference.

Equal-scale cross sections; both plot coordinates are millimetres. The Euler comparison uses the measured longest frame bay and pinned ends. The 0.65 study reduction is included. Local, distortional and torsional instability are excluded.
